title: Pool Service Software: 8 Tools for Routes, Billing and Leads
html:
Pool service software does three jobs: run the route, bill the customer and bring in new pools. Start with one route tool such as Pool Office Manager or Pool Brain. Add QuickBooks or Wave for the books and a free Google Business Profile. Published plans in this guide run from $0 to $299 a month.

Pool service is a route business. A technician visits the same backyards every week, tests water, adds chemicals and logs it. Software for this trade is judged on how fast a tech finishes a stop, not on how many features it lists.

This guide sorts eight tools by the job each one does. Every price comes from the vendor page linked beside it, read in November 2026, and each tool gets one real limit.

Which pool service software is built for routes and water chemistry?

Pool Office Manager and Pool Brain are two tools made for pool routes. Both treat the pool, the equipment and the weekly stop as the unit of work, not a generic job.

  • Pool Office Manager: covers scheduling and dispatch with route optimization, customer and equipment records, water chemistry tracking with dosing suggestions, invoicing and online payments. The first user is $125 a month and each extra active user is $25 a month. Ten technicians come to $350 a month on its own example. There are no per-route or per-customer charges, and it is month to month. Limit: QuickBooks sync is $25 a month extra, and fleet pricing for 12 or more users is not published.
  • Pool Brain: lists one plan with all features and free setup, unlimited office users and a free trial. Field technicians are $65 a month each, shown for up to 5 active techs in the default setup. Limit: the page does not show the base fee or a monthly total, so ask for the full quote before you compare it.

Run the math on your own route before you pick. A three-technician company on Pool Office Manager pays $125 plus two extra users at $25, so $175 a month before add-ons. The same crew on Pool Brain pays $195 for technicians alone, plus a base fee the vendor does not publish.

Pool-built tools win on water chemistry. A tech who logs a chlorine reading and a dosing note at the stop does not rewrite it at night. That one habit saves more office time than any dashboard.

Chemistry logs also protect you in a dispute. When a customer says the water was green all week, a dated reading from the stop settles it. Check that the tool keeps history per pool, not just per customer.

Ask about offline mode too. Many backyards have weak signal, and a tech who cannot save a reading at the stop will write it on paper. Test the mobile app in your worst-signal neighborhood during the trial, before you migrate your whole route.

Finally, count who needs a login. Office staff, owners and technicians are priced differently across these tools, so a cheap two-seat plan can double when a part-time helper joins in summer.

Can general field service software run a pool company?

Yes, if your work is mostly scheduling, invoicing and reminders. Jobber, Housecall Pro and Service Fusion are general field service apps that many pool companies run. None of them is a pool-specific water log, so confirm how each handles recurring weekly stops.

ToolPlan shownPrice shownUsers
Pool Office ManagerOne plan$125 first user, $25 each extraPer tech
Pool BrainOne plan$65 per technician, base fee not shownUnlimited office
Jobber CoreCore$49 monthly, $29 billed annually1
Housecall Pro EssentialsEssentials$149 a month billed annually5
Service Fusion StarterStarter$208 a month billed annuallyUnlimited

Published list prices from each vendor page, November 2026. Taxes, add-ons and card fees are extra.

General apps suit a pool company that also does repairs, openings and one-time cleanups. Those jobs are quotes and visits, which Jobber and Housecall Pro handle well. A weekly route with 150 stops is where a pool-built tool pulls ahead.

Which tools handle pool service invoices and QuickBooks?

QuickBooks Online and Wave are the two accounting tools worth a look, and both take invoices. Most route tools sync to an accounting app, so the books tool is a second purchase, not a replacement.

  • QuickBooks Online: Simple Start is listed at $38 a month, with a 50% promotion for the first three months. Essentials is $85 and allows three users. Plus is $140 and adds project profitability tracking. Limit: Simple Start allows one user, so a bookkeeper plus an owner needs a higher plan.
  • Wave: Starter is $0 and Pro is $19 a month billed monthly. Both allow unlimited estimates and invoices. Card payments on Starter cost 2.9% plus 60 cents. Limit: Wave is invoicing and bookkeeping only, with no routes or scheduling.

Match the accounting tool to how you get paid. Pool companies often bill monthly by card on file. That makes processing fees a real line in the budget, so compare them as closely as the plan price.

Sync matters more than features. If your route tool pushes each paid invoice into QuickBooks, month-end takes minutes. If it does not, you retype every payment, and that is the work you bought software to avoid.

What does a pool service software stack cost each month?

A one-truck pool owner can run a full stack for $125 a month, and a three-tech company lands between $237 and $238 on published prices. These totals add plan fees only, so card fees, texting and taxes come on top.

StackPartsMonthly plan cost
One-truck ownerPool Office Manager first user, Wave Starter, Google Business Profile$125
Three-tech routePool Office Manager with two extra users and QuickBooks sync, QuickBooks Simple Start at list price$238
Three-tech route with repairsJobber Connect for five users billed monthly with no commitment, QuickBooks Simple Start at list price$237

Built from the vendor prices above, November 2026. QuickBooks is shown at list price, before its three-month promotion.

The table leaves out card processing, which is often the biggest hidden cost. Jobber lists 2.9% plus 30 cents per card payment, and Wave lists 2.9% plus 60 cents on Starter. On a $120 monthly service bill that is about $3.78 and $4.08 in fees on each payment.

Pool Office Manager also lists customer texting from $10 a month plus usage, and its usage rates are not shown. If you plan to text customers before each visit, ask for the rate first.

Seasonal pools change the math. Pool Office Manager says seasonal users can be deactivated in the off-season. That matters in northern states where a route shuts down for months, so ask any vendor whether you pay for idle seats.

What should a pool company set up first in new software?

Set up customers, pools and equipment first, because every other feature depends on that record. Rushing the import is the most common reason a tool feels broken in week one.

  • Customer and pool records: address, gate code, pool size, surface type and equipment list for each stop.
  • Recurring route: weekly stops in order, with a service day for each customer.
  • Chemistry templates: the readings your techs take at every stop, so nobody invents a format.
  • Invoice rules: monthly flat rate, per-visit rate and a separate rate for chemical add-ons.
  • Reminders: automatic notes to customers about visits and unpaid invoices.

Run the new tool beside your old method for one route before you move everything. A trial exists for exactly that reason, and Pool Office Manager lists a 30-day trial that needs a card at signup.

Judge every tool on whether it removes those three, not on its feature count.

How do pool companies find new customers beyond software?

Route software does not bring in new pools. A free Google Business Profile and a clear website do that first. Google says you can add or claim your business at no charge, per its own help page.

  • Google Business Profile: puts your pool company in Google Maps and local search with your service area, photos, reviews and phone number. Limit: it needs fresh photos, service posts and review replies to hold its place.

Reviews carry weight in this trade, so learn how to handle a negative review before one lands.

A pool site needs pages for weekly service, green pool cleanups and openings, plus a quote form.

How do you choose pool service software for your route?

Choose pool service software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it log chemistry and equipment per pool, repeat weekly stops, and show the next stop on a phone?

Cost: add the plan price, each technician seat, add-ons such as QuickBooks sync and card fees, then divide by your pool count.

Setup effort: can you import your customer list and rebuild the route in a weekend, or does it need a call with the vendor?

A one-truck owner can start with Pool Office Manager at $125 a month, Wave Starter at $0 and a free Google Business Profile. That is the whole stack. Add a website when calls from the map slow down.

A three-tech company with repair work fits Jobber Connect or Housecall Pro Essentials for quotes and scheduling, with QuickBooks for the books. Test a pool-built tool on one route for the trial period first, since its water log is the part generic apps lack.

Software does not create demand, so pair it with lead sources. Search ads from pool cleaning PPC and rankings from pool cleaning SEO send homeowners to the site.

What is the best software for a pool service company?

There is no single best tool, because it depends on route size and repair work. Pool Office Manager and Pool Brain are built for routes and chemistry. Jobber and Housecall Pro suit mixed repair and cleaning work. Test one on a real route before committing.

How much does pool service software cost?

Published prices in this guide run from $0 for Wave Starter to $299 a month for Housecall Pro Max billed annually. Pool Office Manager lists $125 a month for the first user. Pool Brain lists $65 per technician. Card fees and add-ons cost extra.

Does pool service software work with QuickBooks?

Several do. Pool Office Manager offers QuickBooks Online sync for $25 a month extra. Jobber adds it on Connect, and Housecall Pro adds it on Essentials. Confirm that paid invoices sync both ways before you rely on it for month-end.

Do pool companies need route optimization software?

If you service dozens of pools a week, yes. Route tools cut drive time by ordering stops. Pool Office Manager lists route optimization on its single plan, and Housecall Pro lists routes on Essentials. A small route can run on a simple schedule.

Can general field service apps replace pool-specific software?

For quotes, scheduling and invoices, yes. For water chemistry history per pool, check each app carefully, since general tools may not track dosing readings or equipment. Pool-built tools list chemistry tracking as a core feature. Decide which matters more to your crew.

What should a new pool service business buy first?

Set up a free Google Business Profile and one route tool with a free trial. Use Wave Starter at $0 for invoices. Add a website and paid lead sources after the route fills. Do not buy a full suite before you have steady stops.

Is Google Business Profile free for pool companies?

Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge. It still takes work: photos of finished pools, accurate service areas and replies to every review. Google paid ad products are separate and billed on their own.

Software does not create demand, so pair it with lead sources. Search ads from pool cleaning PPC and rankings from pool cleaning SEO send homeowners to the site.
###
What is the best software for a pool service company?
There is no single best tool, because it depends on route size and repair work. Pool Office Manager and Pool Brain are built for routes and chemistry. Jobber and Housecall Pro suit mixed repair and cleaning work. Test one on a real route before committing.
###
How much does pool service software cost?
Published prices in this guide run from $0 for Wave Starter to $299 a month for Housecall Pro Max billed annually. Pool Office Manager lists $125 a month for the first user. Pool Brain lists $65 per technician. Card fees and add-ons cost extra.
###
Does pool service software work with QuickBooks?
Several do. Pool Office Manager offers QuickBooks Online sync for $25 a month extra. Jobber adds it on Connect, and Housecall Pro adds it on Essentials. Confirm that paid invoices sync both ways before you rely on it for month-end.
###
Do pool companies need route optimization software?
If you service dozens of pools a week, yes. Route tools cut drive time by ordering stops. Pool Office Manager lists route optimization on its single plan, and Housecall Pro lists routes on Essentials. A small route can run on a simple schedule.
###
Can general field service apps replace pool-specific software?
For quotes, scheduling and invoices, yes. For water chemistry history per pool, check each app carefully, since general tools may not track dosing readings or equipment. Pool-built tools list chemistry tracking as a core feature. Decide which matters more to your crew.
###
What should a new pool service business buy first?
Set up a free Google Business Profile and one route tool with a free trial. Use Wave Starter at $0 for invoices. Add a website and paid lead sources after the route fills. Do not buy a full suite before you have steady stops.
###
Is Google Business Profile free for pool companies?
Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge. It still takes work: photos of finished pools, accurate service areas and replies to every review. Google paid ad products are separate and billed on their own.
